newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 5.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- POUND HITS HIGH AGAINST YEN

The pound has risen to its highest level against the yen for three-and-a-half years as Japanese investors bought heavily into sterling amid speculation that interest rates in Britain will rise further. Currency analysts believe the pound has further to rise because it is one of the few currencies in the world offering high and rising rates of return. The demand for sterling is stronger now than at any time since 1990.
-- BIOTECH SETBACK DESPITE NEW DRUG

British Biotech has seen a fall in its share price despite announcing that its cancer treatment drug, marimastat, prolongs victims' lives. The share price fell due to concerns over side-effects of shoulder and arm pains. Drugs analyst at brokerage Yamaichi, Erling Refsum, said the side-effects could be crucial to marimastat's potential. Biotech's finance director James Noble said the data is encouraging, but he is concerned not to raise patients' hopes of the drug.
-- CASH SURGE PUTS CLARKE IN A SQUEEZE

Analysts have warned that interest rates will have to be raised further to damp spending and prevent the economy overheating after news of a surge in the amount of cash circulating in the economy. City professionals believe that rising house prices and evidence of booming conditions in London, leading to a one quarter point rise in bank base rates to six per cent, is not sufficient. They believe Chancellor Kenneth Clarke will be forced to tighten policy again before the next election.
THE TIMES
-- BT AND MCI ADVISERS EXPECTED TO EARN 60 MILLION DOLLARS

It has emerged that if the British Telecom takeover of MCI goes ahead, advisors to the two groups will earn a minimum of 60 million dollars. The London and New York offices of BT's main advisor, Rothschild, is expected to collect the largest portion of the fees. BT have also used Morgan Stanley, and MCI hired Lazards. BT shares soared as the city had its first chance to assess the takeover terms and BT's promise to pay a 35 pence stg a share special dividend, as part of its effort to take full control of MCI for 20 billion dollars.
-- RISE IN HOUSE PRICES TOPS SEVEN PER CENT

Halifax, Britain's biggest lender with 2.5 million borrowers, has said that the recovery in the housing market is gathering pace with prices rising at their fastest rate for more than 30 months. The society says house prices in October rose by 1.6 per cent, which is the largest monthly rise since February 1994. The increase prompted Halifax to increase its forecast for a rise in house prices for the whole year, to seven per cent from five percent.
-- ABF READY TO MAKE ONE BILLION STG ACQUISITION

Chairman and chief executive of Associated British Foods which owns British Sugar and Twinings Tea, Garry Weston, has said the company may spend up to one billion stg on an acquisition. ABF is hoping to buy within the food industry outside Europe, with emphasis on the Far East and North America. Weston ruled out packaged foods and cautioned that the acquisition is unlikely to occur for several months. Analysts say Weston is not likely to buy a quoted company.
THE GUARDIAN
-- AIRLINES PLAN COURT CHALLENGE ON NEW NOISE LIMITS

Plans by the Government to introduce stricter noise limits to protect the environment at Heathrow, Stansted and Gatwick is facing a judicial challenge from the airline industry. The court action is being pursued by the International Air Transport Association, whose general secretary, Pierre Jeanniot, said the regulations are too tough and that the British Government is being unreasonable. British Airways backs the Government's proposals but doubt the new limits are achievable.
-- MUTUAL INSURER RAISES 215 MILLION STG

The life insurer and fund management group Friends Provident have given a clear signal to predators that the company wishes to retain its mutual status by raising 215 million stg of debt stocks. Chief executive Michael Doerr said the new debt stock proved mutuals could still raise money on the market and hinted the company was looking at making an acquisition of its own. The new stock will be held in revenue until a suitable opportunity for expansion came its way.
-- BAT POISED TO INCREASE STAKE IN TROUBLED ITC

The tobacco and financial services group BAT Industries is planning to use the crisis at its troubled Indian subsidiary ITC to take a greater stake in the company. ITC, India's biggest tobacco company which also has hotel and commodity interests, is involved in a foreign exchange scandal. BAT is not concealing its plan to raise its shareholding, from 31.7 per cent, in ITC and last year forced the exit of a former chairman after a boardroom struggle.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- OFTEL TO LOOK AT 13 BILLION STG BT TAKEOVER

AT&T, the giant American rival to British Telecom, has said it will lodge a formal objection with Oftel, the UK telecommunications watchdog, about BT's proposed takeover of MCI. It will take up to one year to gain approval for the deal from competition authorities on both sides to the Atlantic. UK regulator Don Cruickshank will investigate a 13.5 per cent stake in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation which the new global company, Concert, will inherit from MCI.
-- INVESCO VALUES ITS FUNDS AT 150 BILLION DOLLARS

Invesco's announcement that it is taking over the Texas- based AIM for 1.6 billion dollars will create one of the largest fund management groups in the world, controlling 150 billion dollars of funds. The deal values the 72 per cent of the mutual fund group held by AIM founder directors and management at 720 million stg and creates a group in the same league as Britain's biggest independent fund manager, Mercury Asset Management.
-- LEADING CABLE OPERATORS JOIN ANTI-SKY CAMPAIGN

Two of Britain's leading cable companies, Nynex CableComms and Telewest Communications, have attacked Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB, claiming the company is acting anti-competitively in the supply of pay-TV programming in the UK market. This comes despite having signed long-term supply agreements with BSkyB. The operators will reject BSkyB's planned "rate card", which lays out the terms and prices under which Sky's channels are offered on a wholesale basis to the cable industry.
